title: Quiet dequant sink prefill scheduler
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Introduce a 'quiet dequant sink' mechanism and a scheduler that intentionally defers and coalesces small dequant operations during prefill to reduce per-token CPU/GPU overhead for mixed-precision (INT8/FP8) decode paths. The goal is to lower end-to-end tail latency and improve throughput for interactive decodes without changing model numeric semantics. This ticket covers design, microbenchmark harness, kernel glue changes, telemetry gating, and a staged rollout.

Background: current prefill flow triggers frequent small dequant ops (per-layer / per-head) when switching from packed INT8/FP8 activations to FP16 kernels used by some attention microkernels. These per-op transitions create kernel launch overhead, allocator churn, and KV cache pressure that disproportionately impacts short-lived interactive requests.

Proposal summary: implement a lightweight sink buffer paired with a lane-aware scheduler that: (1) accumulates small dequant results in-place when safe, (2) coalesces multiple layer-level dequant writes into a single kernel or CUDA stream synchronization point, and (3) introduces a latency budget heuristic so critical-path decode lanes flush immediately while background lanes flush opportunistically. The design favors a small memory tax (configurable per-tenant) and conservative correctness checks (shape/version stamps) so we can enable the feature for hosted and dedicated deployments behind a runtime flag.

Scope: kernel glue (prefill and attention entrypoints), scheduler heuristics, per-tenant config, telemetry (dequant count, sink flush times, p99 impact), unit and integration tests, benchmark suite updates, and rollout plan.

Success criteria: measurable reduction in per-request overhead on mixed-precision models (target 10% aggregate throughput gain for 1-16 tok requests, and 6-10ms p99 tail reduction on our internal chat benchmark), no regression in correctness or long-tail memory usage, and feature gated telemetry to revert quickly if regression appears.
comments: 2026-03-02: Kickoff sync with runtime, infra, and perf. Agreed to prototype as scheduler + sink buffer in user-space first before adding a dedicated kernel. Action: Marco to sketch warm-up heuristics and API for sink buffer.

2026-03-04: Prototype implemented: user-space sink holds up to 4 layers worth of dequantized activations per lane, flush on cross-lane barrier or when size threshold reached. Microbench harness (bench/quiet_dequant.harness) added. Initial perf: +6% throughput on small interactive traces (avg request length 12 tokens).

2026-03-05: Observed spike in transient GPU memory when many lanes buffered simultaneously in dedicated tests. Decision: add per-tenant memory cap and evict oldest non-critical lane; revisit allocation policy if fragmentation arises. Added label 'memory-risk'.
2026-03-06: PR opened (github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/14286). Patch includes scheduler hooks, sink buffer, and telemetry events (dequant_sink.buffered_layers, dequant_sink.flush_latency_ms).

2026-03-08: Review feedback from IR (kernel team): prefer single fused flush kernel for cases where all coalesced writes share contiguous layout to reduce memcpy overhead. Action: design an optional fused-flush codepath; fall back to multi-write when layout mismatches. Assigned to Sophia for fused kernel prototype.

2026-03-09: PM and Product-design review: product accepts latency/throughput trade-offs provided we keep deterministic flushing for customer-facing SLAs. Added config: 'flush_mode' can be 'immediate', 'budgeted', or 'aggressive' per-deployment.
2026-03-10: Integration test added to nightly: validates checkpoint-replay equivalence (run baseline numeric diff on 200 prompts). No diffs at 1e-5 tolerance so far.

2026-03-11: End-to-end benchmark results on staging (mixed LLaMA-like FP8/INT8 variant): 9.8% throughput increase for 1-16 token traffic pattern, median latency unchanged, p99 improved by 7.3ms. Memory tail increased by 2.1% under synthetic burst; within configured cap. Plan: promote to canary for selected tenants in dedicated region eu-west-1 next week.

2026-03-12: Risk note: on multi-tenant hosts with extreme fragmentation we saw spike in allocator stalls. Mitigation: add fast-path that bypasses sink for buckets with fragmentationScore>0.7; infra to expose fragmentation telemetry. Follow-up ticket to quantify fragmentation thresholds (ENG-774200).
next_steps: Finalize fused flush kernel prototype and land PR for fused path (owner: Sophia)
Add per-tenant configuration and admin toggle in console for canary selection
Run 72-hour canary in eu-west-1 on low-risk tenants and collect telemetry
Add allocator-fragmentation bypass and update documentation for ops runbook
Prepare rollback plan and automated gating to disable feature if p99 or memory regressions exceed threshold
